title: Cloud Connector groups: what they are for, autoscaling names, status and disabling

prose.text: {{auto-created}} {{group-purpose}} A forwarding rule can be scoped to groups: [[cloud-connector.forwarding.criteria]].

prose.label: Group types.
prose.text: {{group-types}} How a Zero Trust Gateway differs from a Cloud Connector: [[cloud-connector.overview.zero-trust-gateways]].

prose.label: Status, disable, delete.
prose.text: {{operational-status}} An Inactive connector has lost contact with its management plane but still processes traffic: [[cloud-connector.insights.connector-status:inactive-meaning]]. {{disable-not-delete}} {{delete-irreversible}} Upgrades of the connectors in a group are staggered within a two-hour window: [[cloud-connector.upgrades:two-hour-staggered]]. Whether a disabled VM keeps running, and whether an autoscaling group maps one-to-one to a Cloud Connector group, is not stated {{gap:status-semantics}}.

checks.do: The group's operational status (Active, Inactive or Disabled) and whether it was disabled, which stops traffic processing.
Whether an autoscaling deployment used an autoscaling template, and a static one a non-autoscaling template.

auto-created.statement: Cloud Connector groups are created automatically when a Cloud Connector is deployed in AWS, Azure, or GCP.

quotes: Cloud Connector groups are automatically created when you deploy a Zscaler Cloud Connector in Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud Platform (GCP).

group-purpose.statement: Groups let you apply policies to a set of deployed Cloud Connectors and upgrade the Cloud Connectors in a group while keeping redundancy during the upgrade.

quotes: Apply policies to a group of deployed Cloud Connectors.
Upgrade Cloud Connectors belonging to a group to maintain redundancy while upgrades are being executed.

autoscaling-names.statement: Autoscaling is called Auto Scaling in the AWS Marketplace, Virtual Machine Scale Sets (VMSS) in the Azure Marketplace, and a Managed Instance Group (MIG) with autoscaling in the Google Cloud Marketplace; the Admin Console's "autoscaling" covers all three, and enabling any of them requires contacting Zscaler Support.

quotes: In the AWS Marketplace, autoscaling is referred to as Auto Scaling. In the Azure Marketplace, autoscaling is referred to as Virtual Machine Scale Sets (VMSS). In the Google Cloud Marketplace, autoscaling is referred to as a Managed Instance Group (MIG) with autoscaling.
In the Zscaler Admin Console, references to autoscaling also refer to Auto Scaling, VMSS, and a MIG with autoscaling. To enable Auto Scaling, VMSS, or a MIG with autoscaling, contact Zscaler Support.

template-match.statement: Deploy an autoscaling group only with an autoscaling (ASG) template, and a non-autoscaling deployment only with a non-ASG template.

quotes: When deploying a Cloud Connector, only deploy an autoscaling group (ASG) with an ASG template or a non-ASG with a non-ASG template.

group-types.statement: The groups list distinguishes two group types, Cloud Connector and Zero Trust Gateway, and can be filtered by cloud (AWS, Azure, GCP) and by whether autoscaling is on.

quotes: Cloud: From the drop-down menu, select AWS, Azure, or GCP.
Group Type: From the drop-down menu, select Cloud Connector or Zero Trust Gateway.
Auto Scaling: From the drop-down menu, select True or False.

operational-status.statement: A Cloud Connector's operational status is Active, Inactive, or Disabled.

quotes: Operational Status: The operational status (i.e., Active, Inactive, or Disabled) of the Cloud Connector.

disable-not-delete.statement: Disabling a Cloud Connector or a group stops traffic from processing; it does not delete the Cloud Connector.

quotes: Disable: Disable an individual Cloud Connector or group of Cloud Connectors, which stops traffic from processing. Disabling a Cloud Connector does not delete it.

delete-irreversible.statement: Deleting a Cloud Connector cannot be undone.

quotes: Delete a Cloud Connector. This action cannot be undone.

status-semantics.title: Effect of Disable on the VM, and autoscaling-group to Cloud Connector group mapping
status-semantics.detail: Unverified legacy statements: disabling "keeps the VM in inventory and the VM running"; "an autoscaling group (ASG / VMSS / MIG) is one Cloud Connector Group". The legacy meaning of Inactive ("enrolled but not currently processing") is corrected by cloud-connector.insights.connector-status:inactive-meaning (no management-plane contact, still processes data), and staggered upgrades are held by cloud-connector.upgrades:two-hour-staggered.
status-semantics.blocks: interpreting an Inactive status and planning a staged disable
